body.statement: Uniformly over \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), \(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\asymp_{\epsilon,\alpha}M\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\). The exact-real interval \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\) attains the upper inequality, and for every \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\le r_{n,d,M}\) so does its certified outward-rounded implementation \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\), up to the same constant order.
body.justification: Expected confidence length, rather than point-risk square root, is the decision-theoretic object governing honest uncertainty quantification.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2, determines a point-risk scale for \(\psi_1\), which transfers to ATE point estimation only through \(prop:zeng-one-arm-to-ate-reduction\), but it does not determine honest expected length. ArmstrongKolesar2021 gives finite-sample optimal ATE intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions with normal known-variance errors, not a frontier for unrestricted discrete cell masses under fixed overlap and the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope.
body.consumer: A sample-size and alphabet-size benchmark for whether saturated adjustment can support substantively informative ATE intervals.
